intro: とか holds things up as examples in casual speech: "things like A, B...". It is vague on purpose: the speaker is giving instances, not a full account, and that vagueness also softens offers and reports.

skills.rule: In casual speech, put とか after each example (AとかBとか) to mean "things like A and B"; unlike や it can follow verbs and whole phrases too.
skills.explain:
とか is the conversational cousin of や and など. It normally follows every item, including the last: 映画とか音楽とかが好き "I like movies, music, that kind of thing". The last とか may be dropped (映画とか音楽が好き), and in speech the particle after the list often goes too.

Unlike や, とか can follow plain-form verbs, adjectives and whole clauses: 休みの日は掃除するとか、買い物に行くとか "on days off I do things like cleaning or going shopping". With a single noun it softens an offer: ジュースとか飲む? "Want some juice or something?" After a clause it reports words vaguely: 明日休むとか言ってた "She said something about taking tomorrow off".

The boundary: や is neutral, joins nouns only, and does not follow the last item. と is a complete list, exactly these things. とか is casual: in reports, essays and formal emails write AやBなど instead. In polite conversation (です・ます) とか is fine but sounds chatty.
patterns: A とか B とか [particle] [verb]
[plain verb] とか [plain verb] とか
[plain clause] とか 言ってた

examples.jp: 寿司[すし]{とか}ラーメン{とか}が好[す]きです。
examples.en: I like things like sushi and ramen.

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]は映画[えいが]{とか}見[み]ます。
examples.en: At weekends I watch movies and stuff.

examples.jp: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]は掃除[そうじ]する{とか}、買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]く{とか}、いろいろです。
examples.en: On my days off I do all sorts of things, like cleaning or going shopping.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは明日[あした]休[やす]む{とか}言[い]ってたよ。
examples.en: Tanaka said something about taking tomorrow off.

contrast.note: や is neutral, joins nouns only, and sits between items (AやB). とか is casual, follows each item (AとかBとか) and can follow verbs and clauses.
AとB names the complete set. AとかBとか gives examples and implies there are more.
など is the neutral or formal "and so on", once at the end. とか is its spoken equivalent and repeats.

mistakes.bad: 暇[ひま]な時[とき]は本[ほん]を読[よ]む{や}ゲームをします。
mistakes.good: 暇[ひま]な時[とき]は本[ほん]を読[よ]む{とか}ゲームをする{とか}しています。
mistakes.note: や joins nouns only. To list actions as examples, use とか (or 〜たり〜たりする).

mistakes.bad: 家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{とか}母[はは]{とか}私[わたし]の三人[さんにん]です。
mistakes.good: 家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{と}母[はは]{と}私[わたし]の三人[さんにん]です。
mistakes.note: A complete, counted list takes と. とか says these are only examples, which clashes with an exact count.

skills.tip: Would "and stuff" or "or something" sound right in casual English? Use とか. Writing formally? Use や...など.
